question:
Using properties of determinants, prove that
$$\begin{vmatrix}x+a & x+b & x+c\\a & b & c\\1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}=0$$
for all real values of $x$, $a$, $b$, and $c$. Hence, evaluate the determinant when $x=4$, $a=-2$, $b=3$, and $c=7$, and explain the relation among its rows.
explanation:
Proof using determinant properties
Let
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}x+a & x+b & x+c\\a & b & c\\1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$$
Apply the row operation $R_1\to R_1-R_2$:
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}x & x & x\\a & b & c\\1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$$
Take $x$ common from the first row:
$$D=x\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\a & b & c\\1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$$
The first and third rows are identical. Therefore,
$$D=0$$

Numerical evaluation
For $x=4$, $a=-2$, $b=3$, and $c=7$,
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}2 & 7 & 11\\-2 & 3 & 7\\1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$$
Applying $R_1\to R_1-R_2$ gives
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}4 & 4 & 4\\-2 & 3 & 7\\1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}=4\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\-2 & 3 & 7\\1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}=0$$

Relation among the rows
In the original determinant, every entry of the first row is obtained by adding $x$ times the corresponding entry of the third row to the second row. Thus,
$$R_1=R_2+xR_3$$
The rows are linearly related, so the determinant is zero.

options.A: Applying $R_1\to R_1+R_2$ produces equal rows, so the determinant is $0$; for the given values it is $0$, and $R_1=R_2-xR_3$
options.B: Applying $R_1\to R_1-R_3$ produces equal rows, so the determinant equals $x$; for the given values it equals $4$
options.C: Applying $R_1\to R_1-R_2$ gives $R_1=(x,x,x)=xR_3$, so the determinant is $0$; for the given values it is $0$, and the original rows satisfy $R_1=R_2+xR_3$
options.D: The determinant equals $abcx$; for $x=4,a=-2,b=3,c=7$, its value is $-168$, so the rows are independent
